epic.intent:
## Outcome
A tracked folder gets a **Capabilities** card. A capability is a third-party, local, model-free command-line tool that hosted agents can use (first users: portless, webreel, dev3000). For each capability the person can see whether it is installed and at which version, install a pinned and verified version after an explicit confirmation, turn it on or off for the folder, and see and stop any process the app runs for it. Hosted chats in a folder where a capability is on receive a short, app-authored paragraph telling the agent the tool exists and how to read its own bundled guide.

This epic builds the shared surface and ships **portless** as its first real capability, so it delivers a tool people use, not only plumbing. With portless on, a dev server started by a hosted agent or by the person gets a stable named address such as `https://myapp.localhost`, and a linked Git worktree gets its own subdomain (`fix-ui.myapp.localhost`), so parallel workers stop colliding on port numbers. The folder page lists the live routes; one click (or one agent `open_in_pane` call) opens a route in the chat's browser pane. A harmless fixture capability still exercises the engine in tests. The webreel and dev3000 epics register their tools on top of this one.

## Confirmed decisions (person, 2026-11-12)
- Deep integration: the app itself starts, tracks and stops capability processes; it is not only a detector.
- Deep integration for portless: the app starts and stops the portless proxy and shows its routes.
- The app offers the full portless HTTPS setup (local certificate authority in the system trust store, port 443, hosts-file sync) behind a disclosed administrator prompt. Plain HTTP without elevation remains available.
- (2026-11-15) The former portless epic is folded into this one as its first real capability; that epic is retired. webreel and dev3000 stay separate epics that require this one.
- Acceptance uses a fixture web app shipped with this repository's tests and Dark Mechanicus's own renderer dev server.

## Evidence inspected (portless)
- portless 0.17.0 (npm, Apache-2.0), 2026-11-08; README states macOS, Linux and Windows with Node.js 24 or later. Commands: `run`, `proxy start|stop`, `trust`, `hosts sync|clean`, `list`, `doctor`, `prune`, `clean`, `mcp`. It is pre-1.0 and its state format can change between releases.
- `src/main/panes/browserPane.ts` `normalizeBrowserUrl` already treats `*.localhost` as local.
- Not yet verified on this machine: the exact Windows elevation behaviour, `--unprivileged` on Windows, and whether Electron's Chromium trusts the portless authority from the Windows store. The portless investigation ticket establishes these before portless is integrated.

## Scope
- A provider-neutral capability descriptor (id, display name, pinned version, package integrity, executable, version probe, optional managed-process spec, instruction paragraph, disclosure text).
- Find on PATH, install into an app-owned private folder under user data (never the repository, never a global install), probe, uninstall.
- A managed child-process service (non-PTY) with bounded output, generation fencing, Stop, and kill-on-quit.
- Per-folder enablement stored machine-locally in the app database; nothing written to `.darkmechanicus/` or the repository.
- Instruction delivery to every hosted chat kind through the existing instructions file.
- Delivery into chat terminals: when a capability is on for a folder, its private executable folder is put on the chat terminal's PATH, so the agent runs the tool by name.

- portless: registered as a capability; proxy lifecycle from the app, route list, doctor output; HTTPS setup and its exact reversal (`hosts clean`, trust removal) as explicit human actions with disclosure; a route picker in the chat browser pane (agents use the existing `open_in_pane`, which already accepts `*.localhost`); agent instructions to use `portless run` for dev servers; this repository's own renderer dev server behind a portless name.

## Non-goals
- No plugin system and no user-defined capabilities: descriptors are compiled into the app.
- No change to the saved agent-desktop epic; whether it later reuses this surface is a separate decision recorded as a comment there.
- No model calls, no credentials, no network access beyond downloading the pinned package from the npm registry after confirmation.
- No `dm` command, MCP tool or pane operation installs, enables, disables or stops a capability; those are desktop actions only. An agent that already has a shell can still run its own package manager: containing a same-user shell is not promised.
- portless: no LAN, Tailscale, ngrok or Cloudflare sharing; no OS startup service install; no edits to the person's project `package.json` scripts by the app; the browser pane does not bypass certificate errors (an untrusted authority shows the normal error).
- Native verification on macOS or Linux: no such machine is available to this project today. Those code paths are unit-tested and the runbook says the feature is verified on Windows only.

## Standards
Only the project Definition of Done gates acceptance. Each ticket writes and runs the tests its Tests section lists.

successCriteria.text: A folder page shows a Capabilities card listing each known capability with its state: not installed, installed with version, on or off for this folder, and running or stopped.

Installing a capability happens only after the person confirms a dialog naming the exact package, version and install location; the downloaded package is checked against a pinned integrity value and a mismatch installs nothing.
A process the app starts for a capability is visible in the card, can be stopped from the card, and is gone after the app quits, verified on Windows by process listing.
A hosted chat started in a folder with a capability on finds the capability paragraph in its instructions and can run the tool by name in its terminal; a chat in a folder with it off has neither.
The dm command list, the MCP tool list and the pane control operations contain no operation that installs, enables, disables or stops a capability; those actions exist only as guarded desktop IPC.
Nothing under the repository or .darkmechanicus/ changes when capabilities are installed, enabled or run.

With portless on, the fixture web app and Dark Mechanicus's own renderer dev server run behind named .localhost addresses; two worktrees of the fixture repository serve at the same time at their own subdomains, and the folder page lists the routes.
A listed route opens in the chat browser pane from the pane's route picker, and an agent opens a route of its folder with the existing open_in_pane operation.

HTTPS setup runs only after the person accepts a dialog naming every system change (certificate authority, port 443, hosts file); declining changes nothing and plain HTTP still works; Remove restores the trust store and hosts file, verified by before and after listings on Windows.

epic.title: Capabilities: install, run and explain third-party agent tools per folder, shipping portless named local URLs

bundle.rationale:
## Approach
A small provider-neutral engine in main (`src/main/capabilities/`) with compiled-in descriptors, a verified private install, a managed process service, delivery into chat terminals, and one folder-page card, shipped with portless as the first real capability. A fixture capability exercises the engine in tests.

portless: investigate first, then register it, run its proxy through the managed process service, read its route list, and surface routes on the folder card and in a menu in the chat browser pane. Agents need no new operation, because `open_in_pane` already accepts `*.localhost`.

## Decisions and why
- **Lockfile install with lifecycle scripts off.** A shipped `package-lock.json` pins every package in the tree by integrity, and `npm ci --ignore-scripts` refuses anything else. Rejected: downloading only the tool's own tarball (dependencies unpinned); a global `npm install -g` (changes the person's machine, version drifts); bundling the tools in the app (licence review and app size for tools most folders never use).
- **The person's own Node.js and npm.** portless and dev3000 need Node.js 24 anyway. Electron's bundled Node is not used to run third-party tools.
- **Machine-local state.** On/off and installs live in the app database, so a pull never turns a tool on.
- **No agent route.** Management is desktop IPC only. The existing agent-desktop epic needed consent because the tool acts on the desktop; these tools act inside the folder, so per-folder on/off by the person is the consent.
- **Person's choice: the app offers full HTTPS setup.** Implemented as snapshot, the tool's own commands, verify, and an exact Remove. The app never answers an operating-system prompt.
- **Plain HTTP is the default mode** so that turning the capability on changes nothing outside the app's private folder.
- **No certificate bypass in the browser pane.** If the authority is not trusted the pane shows the error. Rejected: pinning the portless authority in the pane's session, which would hide a broken setup.
- **Routes come only from `portless run`.** The app does not edit project scripts.
- **Route picker in the pane, not an Open button on the folder card**, because a pane belongs to a chat and the folder page has none.
- **PATH delivery, not wrapper commands.** The agent runs the real CLI and reads its own bundled guide; the app does not re-expose each tool's commands.

## Assumptions to confirm during execution
- `npm ci --ignore-scripts` yields a working install for each real tool. Each tool epic's investigation checks this for its tool.
- A test-only registry switch in unpackaged builds is acceptable for the native smoke.
- portless: `--no-tls` or `--unprivileged` works on Windows without elevation.
- portless: Route output can be read reliably (machine-readable list, or the tool's MCP core profile).
- portless: Electron's Chromium trusts an authority added to the Windows store. If not, HTTPS in the pane is reported as not working and the orchestrator escalates the scope decision before the HTTPS ticket starts.
- portless: The tool works when installed with lifecycle scripts off.

## Risks
- Supply chain: mitigated by lockfile integrity and no lifecycle scripts; the tool still runs as the person once started.
- Orphaned processes on Windows: mitigated by tree kill, generation fencing and a real quit test.
- Overlap with the saved agent-desktop epic, whose DM-542 installs its own runtime. Not changed here; noted as a comment on that epic.
- A setup that cannot be exactly undone: mitigated by the stored snapshot, thumbprint-based verification, and manual undo commands in the runbook.
- portless is pre-1.0 and its state format changes: pinned version, parser fixtures from captured output, error state instead of a crash.
- The HTTPS acceptance step needs the person present; that item is reported blocked rather than passed without it.

## Sequencing
One sprint, one deliverable: portless usable from a folder. Row 1: descriptor, fixture web app. Install, processes and terminal delivery run in parallel off the descriptor; the portless investigation runs off the fixture web app in parallel with the engine. The card joins install and processes. portless registration joins the descriptor, installer, card and investigation; routes join registration and processes; the route UI joins routes and the card; HTTPS joins routes and the investigation; the own-dev-server script follows the investigation. The fixture smoke joins card and delivery; the portless smoke joins the fixture smoke, route UI, HTTPS and the script. Runbooks: capabilities after the card, portless after HTTPS and the capabilities runbook. Critical path: descriptor, install, card, portless registration, routes, HTTPS, portless smoke.

Why one sprint (person, 2026-11-15): the engine without a real tool, and plain-HTTP routes without the HTTPS the person asked for, are not deliverables. The elevation risk is held by ticket order (HTTPS requires routes and the investigation) and the person-present smoke, not by an extra checkpoint.

## Dependencies on other epics
webreel and dev3000 require this epic complete; dev3000 also needs the portless HTTPS setup it ships.

## Verification
Definition of Done once at the acceptance node, real tests for install and process kill, and two native Windows drivers (fixture capability lifecycle; portless routes, worktrees and HTTPS with the person present) with screenshots, certificate-store and hosts listings, and post-quit process listings. macOS and Linux are unit-tested only.

tickets.body:
## Context
A capability is a third-party, local, model-free CLI that hosted agents can use. This ticket fixes the contract the install, process, delivery and UI tickets build on. Nothing here installs or runs anything.

## In scope
- `docs/decisions/0007-capabilities.md` (ADR, same format as 0006). Record: descriptors are compiled into the app (no user-defined ones); installs live in `<userData>/capabilities/<id>/<version>/`, never in a repository and never global; install is `npm ci --ignore-scripts` from a shipped lockfile (see the install ticket); install records and per-folder on/off are machine-local in the app database; management is desktop-only, with no `dm`, MCP or pane route; a same-user shell is not contained.
- `src/shared/desktop/capabilities.ts`: `CapabilityId`, `CapabilityDescriptor` (id, name, summary, packageName, version, minNode, bin: path of the executable inside the install, versionProbe: args and pattern, optional process spec: args, optional stop args, instruction: an app-authored Markdown paragraph, disclosure: lines shown before install) and `CapabilityState`.
- `src/main/capabilities/registry.ts`: the compiled-in list. Production list is empty in this epic. A `fixture` descriptor exists for tests only.
- `src/main/capabilities/store.ts` on the app database: app migration V5 adds `capability_installs` (capability id, version, install dir, installed at) and `folder_capabilities` (canonical folder, capability id, enabled).

## Out of scope
Installing, processes, terminal delivery, UI.

## Source locations
- `src/main/desktop/appDatabase.ts`: `APP_MIGRATIONS` (v1 to v4), `openAppDatabase`. Add `const V5` with a doc comment and append `{ version: 5, sql: V5 }`. Test: `appDatabase.test.ts`.
- `src/main/desktop/folderAgentDefaults.ts`: `createFolderAgentDefaults` is the pattern for a store keyed by canonical folder. Test: `folderAgentDefaults.test.ts`.
- `src/shared/desktop/agentKinds.ts`: `AGENT_DEFINITIONS` is the pattern for compiled-in definitions. Test: `agentKinds.test.ts`.
- `docs/decisions/0006-image-attachments.md`: ADR format.
- New folder `src/main/capabilities/` (does not exist yet).

## Tests
- `src/main/capabilities/store.test.ts`: enable and disable per folder; unknown capability id refused; install record round trip; two spellings of one folder resolve to one canonical row.
- `src/main/desktop/appDatabase.test.ts`: V5 applies to a version 4 database and to an empty one.
- `src/main/capabilities/registry.test.ts`: ids unique; the fixture is absent from the production list; every instruction paragraph is a constant string.

## Verify
Run the three test files, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: Sets the shared contract three later epics build on; several small design choices across shared types, registry and store.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Declining the confirmation dialog changes nothing on disk and nothing in the app database.

A tarball whose bytes do not match the lockfile integrity fails the install and leaves no folder and no record.

tickets.body:
## Context
The design is decided in ADR 0007. Each descriptor ships `resources/capabilities/<id>/package.json` and `package-lock.json` pinning the exact version and an integrity value for every package in its tree. Installing copies both files to a temporary sibling of `<userData>/capabilities/<id>/<version>/`, runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` there with the person's own Node.js and npm, then renames the folder into place.

## In scope
- `src/main/capabilities/findProgram.ts`: find `node` and `npm` on PATH without a shell. On Windows honour PATHEXT (`npm.cmd`). Nothing in `src/main` searches PATH today, so this is new. Refuse a Node.js older than the descriptor's `minNode` with a message that names both versions.
- `src/main/capabilities/installer.ts` (pure, injected deps) and `installerNode.ts` (real spawn and files): confirm, install, probe, record; and uninstall.
- Confirmation is a native dialog, Cancel as default, naming the package, the version, the install folder and every disclosure line of the descriptor.
- After install, run the descriptor's version probe. If the output does not match the pinned version, remove the folder and record nothing.
- Uninstall removes the folder and the record, and is refused while that capability has a running process (take an `isRunning` dependency; the process ticket supplies it).
- A failed or cancelled install leaves no folder and no record.

## Out of scope
Making a tool work that needs its lifecycle scripts: the tool's own epic finds that out and decides. No UI beyond the native dialog.

## Source locations
- `src/main/desktop/agentInstaller.ts`: `createAgentInstaller`, `installDialogOptions`. Follow its order: confirm, fetch, verify, run, locate, probe, record. Test: `agentInstaller.test.ts`.
- `src/main/desktop/agentInstallerNode.ts`: `runInstallerProcess`, `createInstallerFiles`. Test: `agentInstallerNode.test.ts`.
- `src/main/desktop/agentProbe.ts`: `probeAgent`, `planCliLaunch` (Windows shim rules, no shell), `ProcessRunner`. `agentProbeNode.ts`: `runProcess`.
- `src/main/desktop/bootstrap.ts`: `confirmInstall` (native `dialog.showMessageBox`, wrapped in `withNativeOcclusion`).
- `src/main/capabilities/store.ts` and `registry.ts` from the descriptor ticket.
- Test resources: `src/main/capabilities/__fixtures__/` holding a tiny fixture package tarball with a `postinstall` script that writes a marker file, and a lockfile that points at it with `file:`.

## Tests
- `installer.test.ts` (injected deps): declined dialog does nothing; `npm ci` failure leaves no folder and no record; probe mismatch removes the install; success records it; uninstall refused while running; Node.js too old refused.
- `findProgram.test.ts`: PATH order, PATHEXT on Windows, missing program gives null, nothing goes through a shell.
- `installerNode.real.test.ts`: a real `npm ci --ignore-scripts` of the fixture lockfile into a temp folder with no network, and the `postinstall` marker is absent afterwards; the same with a tampered tarball fails.

## Verify
Run the three test files, lint, typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: The app runs a package manager on downloaded code: integrity, no lifecycle scripts and no partial installs must all hold, and a mistake is hard to see.

tickets.body:
## Context
The app has no manager for long-lived child processes outside chat and sign-in terminals. Capabilities such as a local proxy need one that the person can see and stop, and that never outlives the app.

## In scope
`src/main/capabilities/processes.ts`: `createCapabilityProcesses(deps)` with `start(folder, capabilityId, spec)`, `stop`, `status`, `tail`, `subscribe`, `busy()` and `dispose()`.
- `child_process.spawn` without a shell; working directory is the canonical folder unless the spec names another inside it.
- One process per folder and capability. A second start while one runs is refused.
- Output kept in memory only, in a bounded ring (2,000 lines or 256 KiB, whichever comes first); the number of dropped lines is reported. Nothing is written to disk.
- Each start gets a generation number. Exit or output from an older generation is ignored.
- Stop runs the descriptor's stop args first when it has them, with a deadline, then kills the process tree.
- `busy()` and `dispose()` join the existing quit path next to chat terminals.

## Out of scope
IPC and UI (the folder page ticket). Auto-restart.

## Source locations
- `src/main/terminals/loginTerminals.ts`: `createLoginTerminals` is the smallest manager with the `busy()` and `dispose()` shape to copy. Test: `loginTerminals.test.ts`.
- `src/main/agents/processTree.ts`: `killProcessTree`, `startsOwnGroup`. Tests: `processTree.test.ts`, `processTreeReal.test.ts`.
- `src/main/quitDisposal.ts`: `disposeBeforeQuit`. Test: `quitDisposal.test.ts`. Wired in `src/main/index.ts` to `bridge.chats.busy` and `dispose`; compose the new manager there.
- `src/main/desktop/bootstrap.ts`: `startDesktopBridge` is where the manager is created.
- `src/main/desktop/agentProbeNode.ts`: `runProcess` shows the spawn-without-shell pattern.

## Tests
- `processes.test.ts` (fake spawner): second start refused; stale generation ignored; ring bounded and drop count correct; stop escalates to tree kill after the deadline; dispose stops everything; busy is true while one runs.
- `processes.real.test.ts`: a real Node child that starts a grandchild; after stop, and separately after dispose, both process ids are gone.
- `quitDisposal.test.ts`: quit waits for and disposes a busy capability process together with chat terminals.

## Verify
Run the three test files, lint, typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: First long-lived non-terminal child process manager in the app; the hard part is killing the whole tree on Windows and at quit.

tickets.body:
## Context
With private installs the tool is not on the person's PATH. A hosted agent should be able to run it by name, and should be told it exists, only in folders where the person turned it on.

## In scope
When a chat terminal starts or resumes in a folder, for each capability that is both on for that folder and installed:
- prepend the folder that holds its executable to the terminal's PATH (keep the existing entries and the existing key casing on Windows; no duplicate on resume);
- append the descriptor's instruction paragraph to the chat's instructions file, after the collaboration policy and before any run, transfer or Kanban guidance.
The paragraph is the descriptor's constant text. No folder name, route, file content or other external data is interpolated into it.
Sign-in terminals get neither. A custom CLI gets the PATH always and the paragraph only when its arguments use `{instructions}`, as today.

## Out of scope
Any `dm` command or MCP tool about capabilities. Changing instructions of a chat that is already running.

## Source locations
- `src/main/terminals/terminalFiles.ts`: `terminalInstructions` builds the `sections` array; add one push and a new field on `InstructionOptions` and `WriteOptions`. `writeTerminalFiles` writes `<userData>/agents/instructions/<chatId>.md`. Test: `terminalFiles.test.ts`.
- `src/main/terminals/terminalEnv.ts`. Test: `terminalEnv.test.ts`.
- `src/main/terminals/terminalLaunchSpec.ts`. Test: `terminalLaunchSpec.test.ts`.
- `src/main/terminals/terminalSessions.ts`: `createTerminalSessions`. Tests: the `terminalSessions.*.test.ts` family.
- `src/main/terminals/loginTerminals.ts`: must stay unchanged in behaviour.
- `src/main/capabilities/store.ts` from the descriptor ticket supplies what is on and installed.

## Tests
- `terminalFiles.test.ts`: paragraph present only when on and installed; placed after the collaboration text; rewritten on every start; absent after the capability is turned off.
- `terminalEnv.test.ts`: PATH prepend keeps existing entries and the Windows key casing; resume does not add it twice.
- A `terminalSessions` test: a sign-in terminal's environment and files are unchanged.

## Verify
Run the touched test files, lint, typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: Touches terminal environment, instruction assembly and session start for every chat kind, on new start and resume.

tickets.body:
## Context
There is no reusable fixture web app: each native smoke script inlines its own `http.createServer`. The portless, webreel and dev3000 epics all need the same small app with a `dev` script.

## In scope
`scripts/native/fixtures/webapp/`:
- `package.json`: name `dm-fixture-webapp`, script `"dev": "node server.mjs"`, no dependencies.
- `server.mjs`: an HTTP server on `process.env.PORT` (port 0 when unset; print the chosen address on one line), bound to `127.0.0.1` only. It logs one line per request to stdout.
  - `/`: a heading, a button that reveals a line of text, and a text field with a submit button that shows the submitted value.
  - `/boom`: a page whose script throws an uncaught error and fetches `/api/fail`.
  - `/api/fail`: logs `fixture failure requested` and answers 500.
- `start.ts`: `startFixtureWebapp()` for smoke drivers, returning the address and a `stop()`.
Leave the inline servers in the existing smoke scripts as they are.

## Source locations
- `scripts/native/main/browserPane.smoke.ts`: the inline `http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1` port 0 is the pattern.
- `scripts/xtermGraphemesPatch.test.mjs`: where a test for a script lives and how it is named.
- `README.md`, "Commands": native drivers under `scripts/native/` are typechecked and linted.

## Tests
`scripts/native/fixtures/webapp/server.test.mjs`: honours `PORT`; binds loopback only; `/api/fail` answers 500 and logs its line; `stop()` closes the server.

## Verify
Run the test file, lint, typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: The body spells out every route and file.

tickets.body:
## Context

acceptanceCriteria.text: The report answers each of the nine questions with the command, its output, the date and the portless version, and labels each answer observed, read from source, or unverified.
The before and after listings of both certificate stores and the hosts file hash are in the report and show no difference, or an exact restoration.
The report ends with the Integration decisions list covering proxy start and stop, state location, route listing, default HTTP mode, HTTPS setup steps and removal steps.
Every step that was not performed because it needed a prompt answered for the person is named as unverified, with the exact command the person would run.

tickets.body:
## Context
The README says portless runs on Windows with Node.js 24 or later, serves HTTPS on port 443 by creating a local certificate authority in the system trust store, keeps the hosts file in sync, and offers `--no-tls` and `--unprivileged`. None of that has been run on this machine. The later tickets need facts, not the README.

## Questions to answer, each with the command, its output, the date and the version
1. Does `npm ci --ignore-scripts` from a lockfile pinned to `portless@0.17.0` give a working `portless`? Does the package rely on any lifecycle script?
2. `--no-tls` and `--unprivileged` on Windows: which ports, and is any elevation requested?
3. Proxy lifetime: what starts it, is it a background daemon, what does `portless proxy stop` do, where is its state, and which environment variable moves the state?
4. Route listing: is there machine-readable output from `portless list`? If not, what does the `portless mcp` core profile return?
5. Worktrees: the route names for the main checkout and a linked worktree of the same repository.
6. Name resolution: does `myapp.localhost` resolve on Windows for Chromium, for Node `fetch`, and for `curl`, with and without `portless hosts sync`?
7. `portless trust`: which store it writes, which prompt Windows shows, and the exact way to undo it. Read the source at tag v0.17.0 for what cannot be observed without accepting a prompt.
8. After trust (only if step 7 could be completed without accepting a prompt for the person): does the Electron 42 browser pane load an `https://*.localhost` route without a certificate error?
9. How can `electron-vite dev` take the port portless assigns, for this repository's own renderer?

## Safety rules for this ticket
- Before any command that could touch the certificate store or the hosts file, save `certutil -user -store Root` and `certutil -store Root` listings and the SHA-256 of the hosts file. Save them again at the end and diff.
- Read a prompt before answering it. Never send a blind key press to dismiss an unknown prompt. Never accept an administrator or certificate-trust prompt on the person's behalf: stop at the prompt, record it, and mark the step unverified.
- Use a throwaway state location when the tool offers one, and do not install an OS startup service.

## Source locations (entry points; no code change expected)
- `electron.vite.config.ts`: `DEV_SERVER_ORIGIN` (the renderer dev server is `http://localhost:5173`).
- `src/main/panes/browserPane.ts`: `normalizeBrowserUrl` (scheme-less `*.localhost` gets `http`) and the `certificate-error` handler, which always rejects.
- `docs/reports/omp-cli.md`: the report format to follow.
- `scripts/native/fixtures/webapp/` from this epic: the app to run.

## Tests
None: investigation. The evidence is the report.

## Output
`docs/reports/portless-windows.md`, ending with an "Integration decisions" list that the later tickets cite: proxy start and stop commands, state location, route listing method, the default HTTP mode, the HTTPS setup steps and the removal steps. Label every statement observed, read from source, or unverified.

reasoning.rationale: Bounded investigation of a tool that can change system trust and name resolution; needs care about what is observed versus read from source.

tickets.body:
## Context
The person chose to have the app offer the full HTTPS setup behind a disclosed prompt. The app has no elevation code today, and it must not gain a way to answer an operating-system prompt for the person.

## In scope
`src/main/capabilities/portless/https.ts`:
- `plan()`: the exact system changes on this platform, taken from the report: which certificate store gains which authority, which port the proxy binds, which hosts entries are written.
- Setup: a native dialog, Cancel as default, listing every planned change verbatim. On accept: snapshot the current state (certificate thumbprints in the affected store, hosts file hash and the lines portless owns) into the app database, then run the tool's own commands as the person. If Windows shows its own trust or elevation prompt, the person answers it; the app supplies no credential and presses nothing. Verify with `portless doctor`, then record that setup is done.
- If a step fails part-way, undo the completed steps and report what was and was not undone.
- Remove: run the reversal steps, then verify the authority with the recorded thumbprint is gone and the owned hosts lines are gone; report any mismatch.
- IPC for plan, setup, remove and state, desktop only. No agent route.
- The browser pane keeps rejecting certificate errors. No bypass is added.

## Source locations
- `docs/reports/portless-windows.md`: Integration decisions, HTTPS setup and removal steps.
- `src/main/desktop/bootstrap.ts`: native dialogs wrapped in `withNativeOcclusion`; `confirmInstall` is the nearest pattern.
- `src/main/capabilities/processes.ts`, `store.ts` (this epic); `src/main/desktop/appDatabase.ts` for one more app migration holding the snapshot.
- `src/main/panes/browserPane.ts`: the `certificate-error` handler that must stay as it is.

## Tests
`https.test.ts` (injected runner and dialog): declined dialog runs no command; the snapshot is stored before the first command; a mid-way failure undoes completed steps and reports; remove verifies by thumbprint and owned lines; the dialog text contains every planned change; no handler performs setup without the dialog. A `browserPane.test.ts` case asserts a certificate error is still rejected.

## Verify
Run the tests, lint, typecheck. The real setup and removal are exercised in the smoke ticket with the person present.

reasoning.rationale: Changes system trust and name resolution on the person's machine; the order of snapshot, change, verify and undo must be right and a wrong call is costly.
